note: The backward edge, two hops. breaker.ts is in the seed and taints shared.ts forward; shared.ts then taints sibling.ts backward because sibling.ts captured its registry object. Nothing in sibling.ts predicts its own verdict, which is why a fallback report has to be able to name the capture. The captured value is a plain object, which F-Identity's reference test admits and its entity test would not: the edge exists here because F-Capture over-approximates on purpose.
